test: Literal reversed-pronunciation same-meaning search with vertical-language follow-up
question: Do any directionally eligible LTR/RTL languages contain same-meaning words whose phone order literally reverses across languages, and do those concepts then align in the top-to-bottom language?

design.horizontal: For each same-meaning LTR/RTL word pair, reverse the LTR phone sequence itself, then compute phonetic-feature edit distance to the RTL word. No geometric reflection or arbitrary transform is allowed.
design.controls: Each real meaning is compared with 20 wrong meanings in the RTL language. Reverse-vs-direct improvement is also required for the strongest hits.
design.pair_search: All eligible LTR languages are tested against the eligible RTL language; 2000 label permutations correct for choosing the best horizontal pair.
design.hit_freeze: The strongest 10% of concepts that both beat wrong meanings and improve under literal reversal are frozen before looking at the vertical language.
design.vertical: For the frozen horizontal reversal hits only, the Korean/TB word is rotated by the fixed TB coordinate transform from the earlier alphabet test and compared with the midpoint phonetic path of the reversed-LTR and RTL words.
design.vertical_control: Each true vertical meaning is compared with 20 wrong vertical meanings and 2000 label permutations.
design.support: A linked three-way signal would require a horizontal reverse effect that survives pair-search correction and a positive vertical follow-up with p<0.05 on the frozen horizontal hits.
